definitions.explanation: A wire or cable used to transmit electricity. Includes both overhead power lines and electrical wiring.

examples.japanese: {電線|でんせん}に{鳥|とり}がとまっている。
examples.english: A bird is perching on the power line.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{電線|でんせん}が{切|き}れた。
examples.english: The power line was severed by the typhoon.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{電線|でんせん}を{地下|ちか}に{埋|う}める{工事|こうじ}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: In this area, work is underway to bury the power lines underground.

notes:
{電線|でんせん} refers to wires or cables that carry electricity, including both overhead power lines and building wiring.

FORMS:
{電|でん} (electricity) + {線|せん} (line/wire)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電線|でんせん}が{切|き}れる (power line snaps)
- {電線|でんせん}を{引|ひ}く (to run electric wire)
- {電線|でんせん}に{触|さわ}る (to touch a wire — dangerous)
- {電線|でんせん}を{地中|ちちゅう}に{埋|う}める (to bury power lines underground)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Overhead power lines and utility poles ({電柱|でんちゅう}) are a characteristic feature of Japanese cities. There is an ongoing government effort called {無電柱化|むでんちゅうか} (utility pole elimination) to bury lines underground.

RELATED WORDS:
- {電柱|でんちゅう}: utility pole
- {送電線|そうでんせん}: transmission line (high-voltage)
- {配線|はいせん}: wiring (inside buildings)
